name: Domain Recon
summary: Enriches Domain nodes with DNS records (A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, NS, TXT, CAA), RDAP registration data, and Certificate Transparency subdomains from crt.sh and crt.name (desktop only).
description:
Domain Recon fills in what public infrastructure records say about the Domain nodes already in a graph: their DNS records, their registration data, and the subdomains that appear in Certificate Transparency logs. It needs no API key or account. Nine of its ten plugins run in the browser; the crt.name plugin needs the Vineyard desktop app.

Every plugin runs on the selected Domain nodes, reads their `domain_name`, and skips anything else in the selection.

## Plugins

### DNS Lookup (A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, NS, TXT and CAA Record)

Seven plugins, one per record type, so a run asks only for the records wanted. Tick several in the Run dialog to run them together over the same selection.

| Plugin | Adds | Edge from the Domain |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DNS Lookup (A Record) | IP Address nodes (IPv4) | `resolves to` |
| DNS Lookup (AAAA Record) | IP Address nodes (IPv6) | `resolves to` |
| DNS Lookup (CNAME, MX, NS, TXT or CAA Record) | DNS Record nodes with `record_name`, `record_type` and `record_value` | `has record` |

- An IP Address node is shared by every domain that resolves to it, so two domains on one host meet at one node.
- A DNS Record node belongs to one domain: it is identified by name, type and value together. A common value, such as a hosted mail provider's MX or a shared SPF string, does not join unrelated domains into one hub.
- MX values keep the host and drop the preference number. NS and CNAME hosts are lowercased and lose the trailing dot. TXT and CAA values are kept as returned, apart from quotes that wrap the whole value.
- Queries go over DNS-over-HTTPS to Cloudflare, and to Google only when Cloudflare's resolver fails.

### RDAP Domain

Writes the selected Domain's `registrar`, `created_date`, `expiration_date` (YYYY-MM-DD), `status` and `name_servers` from RDAP, the structured replacement for WHOIS. Creates no nodes. Only the fields RDAP returned are written; a field it did not return is left as it was. The lookup goes to rdap.org, which redirects to the RDAP server of the domain's registry. A domain the registry does not know, or whose TLD has no RDAP service, is skipped.

### Certificate Transparency Subdomains

Finds subdomains of each selected Domain in Certificate Transparency logs through crt.sh and adds them as Domain nodes linked `subdomain`. Names come from each certificate's Subject Alternative Names and common name; a leading `*.` is removed and only names under the queried domain are kept. Up to 150 subdomains per domain; the run summary says how many more were left out. crt.sh sometimes answers with a non-JSON error page under load, and that domain is then skipped for the run.

### Certificate Transparency Subdomains (crt.name)

The same search against a second source, crt.name, for when crt.sh is slow, down, or thin for a domain. Every subdomain crt.name returns is added; there is no per-domain cap. crt.name allows 1,000 requests a day per IP address; a domain refused for the quota is skipped and counted in the run summary.

**Desktop only.** crt.name sends no CORS headers, so a browser cannot read its answer; the desktop app makes the request itself. In the browser the plugin stops with a message saying so.

## Requirements

- No API key, token or account.
- Certificate Transparency Subdomains (crt.name) needs the Vineyard desktop app. The other nine plugins work in the browser and in the desktop app.

## Cost and limits

The services used are free. Two limits apply:

- crt.sh: at most 150 subdomains per domain, a cap set by this pack to keep the graph reviewable.
- crt.name: 1,000 requests a day per IP address, set by crt.name.

## What it contacts

Requests go directly from the analyst's browser or desktop app; no Vineyard server is involved. Each service sees the domain names looked up and the analyst's IP address.

| Plugin | Service |
| --- | --- |
| DNS Lookup (all seven) | https://cloudflare-dns.com/dns-query, and https://dns.google/resolve as fallback |
| RDAP Domain | https://rdap.org/, then the registry RDAP server it redirects to |
| Certificate Transparency Subdomains | https://crt.sh/ |
| Certificate Transparency Subdomains (crt.name) | https://crt.name/ |

Nothing is sent to the domain's own web or mail servers. A DNS resolver that has no cached answer asks the domain's authoritative name servers, as any resolver does; that query comes from the resolver, not from the analyst.

## Source

https://github.com/Vineyard-Intelligence/pluginpack-domain-recon

Licensed Apache-2.0. The bundle `dist/pack.mjs` is built from `src/` with a pinned esbuild, so it can be rebuilt and compared with `node build.mjs && git diff --exit-code dist/pack.mjs`.
